programmeGates.title: Loop 03's mandated run state machine contradicts Loop 01's frozen contract
programmeGates.detail: Roadmap Loop 03 §4 specifies a MINIMUM ('tối thiểu') run state machine: draft, queued, running, waiting_user, waiting_external, paused, succeeded, failed, cancelled. W1's frozen RunState is: created, queued, running, awaiting_approval, paused, completed, failed, canceled. Four differences are naming only, but waiting_external is genuinely ABSENT and W1's mapping §3.4 explicitly declined to add it.
programmeGates.analysis: W1's reasoning was sound for the question it asked — which legacy values force a new state — but that is a migration question, not a product requirement. Two pieces of evidence W1 did not weigh: (1) the roadmap calls the list a minimum, so Loop 03's acceptance is measured against it; (2) Loop 02 §3 requires the Today page to show Active work / Waiting for me / Delivered as distinct lanes, and a run blocked on an integration or runtime is none of those three. Under W1's model that run is 'paused' plus an OPTIONAL pausedReason, and a primary always-visible product lane cannot be built reliably on an optional field — any writer that omits it silently misfiles the run, and the state machine cannot enforce legal transitions on a field it does not model.
programmeGates.ruling: CONTRACT CHANGE REQUEST W0 → W1. Add waiting_external as a first-class RunState with transitions running → waiting_external and waiting_external → running | canceled, mirroring paused. Keep pausedReason as an additive detail for the genuinely reason-shaped causes (stuck, guardrail). Keep W1's identifiers for the other four differences: awaiting_approval (W1 §3.3 rejected the rename with evidence), completed/canceled (US spelling matches the codebase), created (W1 §3.7 establishes draft as a WORKSPACE state, and two entities using draft for different lifecycles would be worse).
programmeGates.cost: A version note plus W1 re-running its own tests. This is a breaking change to an UNSHIPPED contract, so there is no migration cost — today.
programmeGates.consequenceIfDeferred: Loop 03 either violates its own acceptance criteria or forks the state machine, which is precisely the failure PQ-08 was raised to prevent.
programmeGates.sequencingConstraint: Must be resolved TOGETHER WITH PO-VERSION-COLLISION and before Loop 03 persists anything. If waiting_external lands after PERSONAL_OFFICE_SCHEMA_VERSION has tagged persisted rows, the version stops being a reliable discriminator.
programmeGates.closureEvidence: W1 accepted the contract change request rather than rejecting it. Verified in the accepted tree: entities.ts RunState includes waiting_external; state-machine.ts models running -> waiting_external and waiting_external -> running | canceled; RunPauseReason narrowed to 'stuck' | 'guardrail'. state-machine.test.ts covers both the legal transitions and the illegal ones (waiting_external -> paused|completed|failed, created/awaiting_approval -> waiting_external). 45/45 tests pass under W0's own run. Cost was a version note only, as predicted — PERSONAL_OFFICE_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1 because no shipped build carries v1.
